subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw add a core Telegram/ACP action-verification or response-gating policy for success claims, or leave claim verification to plugins while only fixing narrower delivery-loss cases in core?
rationale: The behavior spans message delivery, private final text, tool ledger semantics, and plugin extensibility, and changing defaults could alter existing `message_tool_only` privacy and delivery contracts.

options.title: Define a bounded core gate
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved core policy for source turns that can warn, retry, or fail closed when visible success text is not backed by completed delivery/action evidence.

options.title: Keep core diagnostics and route verification to plugins
options.body: Document current delivery semantics and rely on hook-based or ClawHub/plugin claim-verification for workflow-specific action truth.

options.title: Track only the narrower delivery fallback
options.body: Leave this issue open but make #85714/#99536 the only core fix for omitted `message` tool replies, with arbitrary claim verification deferred.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded core gate
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved core policy for source turns that can warn, retry, or fail closed when visible success text is not backed by completed delivery/action evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is product policy across core delivery, privacy, and plugin ownership rather than a single mechanical code owner decision.
